text.p: Texaco Inc chairman and Chief Executive Peter Bijur said on Wednesday he suspended two current employees and the benefits of two retirees allegedly involved in a plan to destroy documents in a discrimination lawsuit against the company.

Bijur, responding publicly for the first time to a scandal that rocked the company this week over allegations of racism and plans to dispose of evidence, told a news conference Texaco was taking six steps to reinforce company policy and code of conduct.

Audiotapes recorded in 1994 in which Texaco executives allegedly discussed destroying evidence and used expletives and racist terms such as "black jelly beans" and "niggers" to belittle black employees became public in the discrimination lawsuit seeking sanctions against Texaco.

"I have just today listened to those tapes myself," Bijur said. "I can tell you that the statements on the tapes arouse a deep sense of shock and anger in me and among all of the members of the Texaco family and decent people everywhere."

Bijur apologized for the remarks heard in the tapes and said two current employees had been suspended immediately with pay and that the medical, insurance and financial benefits of two former employees had also been suspended.

Among the measures Bijur announced to reinforce Texaco policy included visits by senior executives to company locations to apologize to employees; expanding Texaco's "diversity learning experience"; and re-emphasizing respect for the law.
"They are statements that represent a profound contempt, not only for the law but for Texaco's explicitly clear values and policies," Bijur said.

Attorney Daniel Berger, who represents black employees who sued Texaco in 1994 for alleged discrimination, said on Tuesday he had been told that the U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York had started a criminal investigation.
Bijur said Texaco had been subpoenaed in a grand jury probe and that "we are cooperating obviously and complying to the nth degree with all the investigations that are going on."
He said that he expected a separate investigation by an outside lawyer to be completed by the end of this week.
Texaco said the suspended employees were Peter Meade, assistant general manager in the fuel and marine marketing department and David Keough, chief financial and advising officer.

The former employees whose benefits were cut off were former Treasurer Robert Ulrich and Richard Lundwell, senior coordinator of personnel services. Ulrich retired in March 1995 and Lundwell retired five days ago.

New York State Comptroller H Carl McCall, the sole trustee of the state's common retirement fund that owns more than 1.2 million Texaco shares, wrote to Bijur on Wednesday, saying "Your strong and prompt response to alleged remarks and actions of four Texaco employees is a very clear signal of your refusal to tolerate this type of behavior."
